definition_zh: 独一无二的；唯一的；独特的；极好的；罕见的
definition_en: being the only one of its kind, or unusually special and good
core_image: 一整块原石被凿成一只瓶，世上再没有第二只，连模具也没有留下来
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里放着一只烧坏的窑变瓷瓶，釉色在灯下像流动的水。The curator says this unique piece cannot be copied, even by the same kiln.
sceneCN: 这里 unique 是「独一无二的」（第 1 个义项：同类中仅此一件）；句意为馆长说这件孤品即使同一座窑也复制不出来。柜中那只没有第二件的瓷瓶，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「独特地；唯一地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「独特性；唯一性」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「唯一性」（较少用）

senses.title: The only one of its kind
senses.definition: existing as the single example of its kind, so that nothing else is the same
senses.definitionCN: 作为同类中的唯一存在，没有别的东西与它相同
senses.example: Each fingerprint is unique, even between identical twins.
senses.exampleCN: 每个指纹都是独一无二的，即使同卵双胞胎之间也不同。
senses.why: Latin unus means one: the word points to a class with only one member.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」：这个词所指的那一类里只有一名成员。

senses.title: Belonging to one thing only
senses.definition: belonging to or found in only one place, person, or group
senses.definitionCN: 只属于或只出现在某一个地方、人或群体
senses.example: This dialect is unique to a few fishing villages on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方言只存在于沿海几个渔村。
senses.why: Uniqueness can be claimed for a thing by pointing at the one place it occurs.
senses.whyCN: 只要指出它唯一出现的地方，就能为某物主张独有性。

senses.title: Unusually special
senses.definition: unusually good, special, or rare, so as to seem unlike anything else
senses.definitionCN: 格外好、特别或罕见，以至于显得不同寻常
senses.example: She has a unique gift for making shy children speak.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一种难得的天赋，能让害羞的孩子开口说话。
senses.why: Marketers and speakers stretch the word from only one to one of a kind in quality.
senses.whyCN: 广告与演讲把这个词从「只有一个」扩展到「品质上独一类」。

senses.title: The one thing itself
senses.definition: a rare noun use for the single object or person that has no match
senses.definitionCN: 少见的名词用法，指没有相配之物的那一个对象或人
senses.example: Collectors speak of the unique, the piece that no museum can pair.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏家会说起「孤品」，那种任何博物馆都配不成对的物件。
senses.why: Adjectives for state are often turned into nouns, and this one names the matchless thing.
senses.whyCN: 表示状态的形容词常转作名词，这个词指那件无从配对之物。

senses.title: As a key in systems
senses.definition: in computing, identifying one record or account and no other
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，指只标识一条记录或一个账户而不标识其他
senses.example: Every account is given a unique number that is never reused.
senses.exampleCN: 每个账户都被分配一个从不重复使用的唯一编号。
senses.why: Machines need the strict sense: one identifier, one record, no exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 机器需要最严格的意义：一个标识对应一条记录，没有例外。

intro.en: Unique comes from a Latin word built on one, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: unique 来自一个以「一」为核心构成的拉丁语词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Unus meant one, and the adjective unicus meant single, sole, of one only.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，形容词 unicus 意为「唯一的、单独的」。

items.en: French took unicus as un, and formed univ meaning only one, the source of the English word.
items.cn: 法语把 unicus 化约成 un，并构成 univ，义为「只有一个」，是英语词的来源。

items.en: Sixteenth-century French unique was used for the sole example of a thing, with no rival.
items.cn: 十六世纪的法语 unique 用于指某物唯一的实例，没有对手。

items.en: English borrowed the word for things that stand alone in their class, from coins to paintings.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，指在其类别中单独存在的对象，从钱币到绘画。

items.en: The weaker sense of merely unusual or very good spread in advertising and everyday praise.
items.cn: 「仅仅罕见或很好」这种较弱的意义在广告与日常赞美中扩散开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the one root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of rarity and distinction at different strengths.
note.cn: 形近组收以「一」这一词根构成的词；近义组收表示稀有与出众的形容词，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a way that belongs to no other.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「独特地、唯一地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being the only one of its kind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「独特性、唯一性」。

entries.definition: Speaking or singing at the same pitch together; it shares the one but not the sole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「齐声、同音」，共享「一」而不含「唯一」。

entries.definition: A single thing or measure treated as one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「单位、单元」，即被当作一个的整体。

entries.definition: The joining of separate things into one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「联合、工会」，把分开之物合成一个。

entries.definition: Exceptional or odd; in grammar, one rather than many.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非凡的、奇特的」，语法中表示单数。

entries.definition: The only one there is, as in the sole owner; narrower and more legal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「唯一的」，如唯一所有人，范围更窄、更偏法律。

entries.definition: Not often found; it does not claim that only one exists.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稀少的」，并不主张只有一件。

entries.definition: Easy to tell apart from others; about difference rather than number.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有特色的」，强调区别而非数量。

entries.definition: Having no equal at all; a stronger, more formal claim than unique.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无与伦比的」，比 unique 更强、更正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin one at the centre of the word and the phrases it really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词核心处的拉丁语「一」，以及它真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- is one: a unique thing is a class with a single member.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」：unique 之物就是只有一个成员的那一类。

normal.en: Fingerprints are the textbook example: unique even for twins.
normal.cn: 指纹是教科书式的例子：连双胞胎之间也独一无二。

normal.en: Unique to means found in one place only.
normal.cn: unique to 意为只存在于某一处。

normal.en: The word has no true comparative in strict use: something cannot be more one of a kind.
normal.cn: 严格来说这个词没有真正的比较级：一样东西不能更「独一份」。

normal.en: In computing a unique number may never be reused.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，唯一编号绝不可以重复使用。

abstract.en: Picture a key cut for one lock only: no copy of the blank exists, so the key is its own justification.
abstract.cn: 想象一把只为一把锁配出的钥匙：坯子没有第二份，钥匙本身就说明了一切。

abstract.en: Uniqueness is a relation, not a quality: a thing is unique only when compared with the whole class.
abstract.cn: 独特性是一种关系而非性质：只有与整个类别相比，一样东西才成立为唯一。

abstract.en: Advertising loves the word because it turns rarity into worth.
abstract.cn: 广告喜欢这个词，因为它把稀有变成了价值。

examples.en: This valley has a unique climate, with rain on one side and dry wind on the other.
examples.cn: 这条山谷的气候独一无二，一侧多雨，另一侧却是干风。

examples.en: The custom is unique to the islanders.
examples.cn: 这一习俗为岛上居民所特有。

examples.en: Each ticket carries a unique code for entry.
examples.cn: 每张票都带有一个入场专用的唯一编码。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼克」——优尼这一款只有一件，克数也不重样：独一无二

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」所生的 unicus「唯一的、单独的」，经古法语与法语 univ 进入英语；本义是「同类中仅此一件」，近代又扩展出「罕见、极好」的较弱意义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unique all turn on the number one: one member of a class, one place of origin, one of a kind in quality, the matchless object itself, or one key in a system.
sensesIntro.cn: unique 的五个义项都围绕「一」：类别里只有一员、只出现在一处、品质上独一类、那件无从配对之物本身，或系统中唯一的一把钥匙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single vessel fired once, with no mould left and no second copy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只只烧过一次的瓷器，模具没有留下，也没有第二件。

branches.en: THE CLASS: the word marks a class with only one member.
branches.cn: 类别线：这个词标记一个只有一名成员的类别。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the one location or group that has it.
branches.cn: 地点线：拥有它的那唯一一处地方或人群。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: rarity turns into praise of quality.
branches.cn: 赞美线：稀有转为对品质的赞美。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the matchless thing can be named as a noun.
branches.cn: 物件线：那件无从配对之物可用名词来命名。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: machines need one number for one record.
branches.cn: 系统线：机器需要一号对一记录。

intro.en: Unique is almost all root: a Latin word for one, plus a small adjective ending and English suffixes.
intro.cn: unique 几乎全是词根：一个拉丁语「一」词，加一个小小的形容词词尾与英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Unus and unicus are both recorded Latin words, so nothing in the core is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus 与 unicus 均有文献记录，核心部分不需要重构。

items.example: The prefix is the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀是这个词的核心。

items.example: Latin unicus carried this ending into French.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 unicus 带着这个词尾进入法语。

items.example: A French cousin on the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根上的法语近亲。

items.example: An English word built on the same one.
items.exampleCN: 以同一个「一」构成的英语词。

definition_zh: 普遍的；全体的；通用的；宇宙的
definition_en: true of or shared by everyone or everything, or able to be used in all cases
core_image: 一张巨大的圆顶把天南地北的人与物全罩在里面，没有一处露在边缘之外
scene: 孩子们在课堂上争论笑容是不是人人都懂，老师让全班用自己的语言演示同一个表情。Smiling appears to be universal across every culture.
sceneCN: 这里 universal 是「普遍的、人人都有的」（第 1 个义项：对所有人都成立）；句意为微笑似乎在所有文化中都是普遍的。罩住一切的那个圆顶，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 普遍的；全体的；人人都有的
普遍概念；通用规律（哲学用法）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；人人皆然地」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「普遍性；通用性」
与本词同源，义为「宇宙；全体」
与本词同源，义为「大学」，原指师生的全体团体

senses.title: True of everyone
senses.definition: applying to or shared by all people or all things of a kind
senses.definitionCN: 适用于某类的所有人或所有事物，或为其所共有
senses.example: The desire for safety is universal among parents.
senses.exampleCN: 对安全的渴望在父母心中是普遍的。
senses.why: Unus is one and versus is turned towards one: the whole field is gathered into a single reach.
senses.whyCN: unus 是「一」，versus 是「朝向一个」：整片领域被收进同一个范围。

senses.title: Usable in all cases
senses.definition: designed to work or apply in every case, without special adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 无需特别调整即可在任何情形下使用或适用
senses.example: A universal charger saves travellers from carrying five cables.
senses.exampleCN: 一只通用充电器让旅客不必带五根线。
senses.why: The adjective extends from people to tools: one form that fits everything.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从人扩展到工具：一种形式适合一切。

senses.title: Of the whole universe
senses.definition: relating to the whole of space and everything in it
senses.definitionCN: 与整个空间及其中的一切有关的
senses.example: Gravity is a universal force, acting on every mass in space.
senses.exampleCN: 引力是一种宇宙之力，作用于太空中的每个质量。
senses.why: In philosophy the word already meant the whole of things, and astronomy borrowed that reach.
senses.whyCN: 在哲学中这个词本已指万物的全体，天文学借用了这份范围。

senses.title: A general concept
senses.definition: in philosophy, a quality or concept said of many things rather than of one
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中指可被多个事物共有的性质或概念，而非单个事物
senses.example: Medieval thinkers argued about whether universals exist apart from things.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪思想家争论普遍概念是否存在于事物之外。
senses.why: Logic needs a name for what many share, and the word for whole becomes that name.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要为众多事物共有之物命名，表示「全体」的词就成了这个名字。

senses.title: Everyone, without exception
senses.titleCN: 全体一致的；无一例外的
senses.definition: in phrases such as universal approval, agreeing by all without a single objection
senses.definitionCN: 在 universal approval 等说法中，指全体同意、没有一票反对
senses.example: The new playground won universal approval at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 新游乐场在会上获得一致赞同。
senses.why: Here the word does not describe a law but counts people: nobody is left outside.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词不描述规律而在数人：没有一个人被留在外面。

intro.en: Universal is built on the same Latin pair as universe: one, and turning towards one whole.
intro.cn: universal 与 universe 建立在同一对拉丁语词上：「一」，以及「转向同一整体」。

items.en: Unus meant one, and the verb vertere meant to turn; the pair gave universus, turned into one, whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，动词 vertere 意为「转动」；二者合出 universus，即「合成一个、整个的」。

items.en: Late Latin universalis meant belonging to all, and it was the adjective used in logic and law.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 universalis 意为「属于全体的」，是逻辑学与法学里的形容词。

items.en: French universal carried the sense of general and applied to all cases.
items.cn: 法语 universal 带有「一般的、适用于一切情形」的意思。

items.en: Scholastic writers used universal for concepts shared by many things.
items.cn: 经院作者用 universal 指众多事物共有的概念。

items.en: Natural science took up the word for laws holding everywhere, and everyday speech took it for what everyone shares.
items.cn: 自然科学取它表示处处成立的定律，日常言语则取它表示人人共有之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same one-and-turn root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of scope with different breadth.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「合一」词根上的词；近义组收表示范围的形容词，宽窄不同。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning by everyone or in every case.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「普遍地、人人皆然地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of applying to all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「普遍性、通用性」。

entries.definition: Everything that exists, literally turned into one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宇宙」，字面即「合为一体」。

entries.definition: A place of higher learning, once a whole community of scholars.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大学」，原指学者的全体团体。

entries.definition: The belief that a principle holds for everyone everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「普遍主义」，认为某原则对天下所有人成立。

entries.definition: True in most cases but allowing exceptions; weaker than universal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一般的」，多数情形成立但允许例外，比 universal 弱。

entries.definition: Covering the whole world in space or reach.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全球的」，指在空间或影响上覆盖整个世界。

entries.definition: Found over a large area or among many people, but not necessarily all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广泛的」，地域或人群范围大，但不一定涵盖全部。

entries.definition: Shared by many or occurring often; it makes no claim about everyone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「共同的、常见的」，不主张对人人成立。

entries.definition: Broad in taste or interest, or universal in the older sense; formal and rare.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广泛的、普遍的」，较正式而少见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin pieces, one and turn, and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用两个拉丁部件「一」与「转」，以及这个词真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- is one and verse is to turn: turned into one, so everything is inside.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，verse 是「转」：转成一整个，所以一切都在里面。

normal.en: A universal truth holds for everyone, without exceptions.
normal.cn: 普遍真理对每人都成立，没有例外。

normal.en: A universal charger replaces a bag of cables.
normal.cn: 通用充电器能替掉一包线。

normal.en: University and universe share the root: one whole of students, one whole of things.
normal.cn: university 与 universe 共享词根：学生的整体，与万物的整体。

normal.en: Universal approval means not one hand stayed down.
normal.cn: 一致赞同意味着没有一只手没举起来。

abstract.en: Picture a dome wide enough to cover every town at once: whatever stands outside it is, by definition, an exception.
abstract.cn: 想象一个宽到能同时罩住每座城镇的圆顶：站在外面的事物按定义就是例外。

abstract.en: To call a rule universal is a strong claim; one counterexample is enough to break it.
abstract.cn: 称一条规律为普遍的是很强的断言：一个反例就足以打破它。

abstract.en: The word gathers a whole world into one turning point, which is why it can cover laws and people alike.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一整个世界收进同一个转折点，因此它既能盖住规律，也能盖住人。

examples.en: Music is often called a universal language.
examples.cn: 音乐常被称为一种通用语言。

examples.en: Access to clean water should be a universal right.
examples.cn: 获得干净的水应当是一项普遍权利。

examples.en: The plan met with universal support at the council meeting.
examples.cn: 这项计划在议会上得到了全体支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼沃索」——优尼把沃索全部转进一个圈：普遍的、全体的

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」加 vertere「转动」构成的 universus「合成一个的、整个的」，晚期拉丁语 universalis「属于全体的」经法语进入英语；由「全体」引申出普遍、通用与宇宙等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of universal all describe one reach: a whole gathered into one, whether it is all people, all cases, all of space, a shared concept, or a vote without exception.
sensesIntro.cn: universal 的五个义项都描述同一种覆盖：把整体收成一个，无论那是所有人、所有情形、整个空间、共有概念，还是无一例外的表决。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vast dome that encloses every place and leaves nothing outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个巨大的圆顶罩住每一处，什么都不留在外面。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: a feeling or truth shared by everyone.
branches.cn: 人群线：人人都共有的感受或真理。

branches.en: THE TOOL: one design that fits every case.
branches.cn: 工具线：一种设计适用于每一种情形。

branches.en: THE COSMOS: the reach extends to all of space.
branches.cn: 宇宙线：覆盖范围扩展到整个空间。

branches.en: THE CONCEPT: philosophy names what many things share.
branches.cn: 概念线：哲学为众多事物共有之物命名。

branches.en: THE VOTE: nobody is left outside the agreement.
branches.cn: 表决线：没有人被留在同意之外。

intro.en: Universal is a Latin compound plus an adjective ending, with English suffixes for its family.
intro.cn: universal 是一个拉丁语复合词加形容词词尾，家族成员用英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Unus, vertere and universus are all recorded, and universalis is recorded in late Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus、vertere、universus 均有记录，universalis 见于晚期拉丁语。

items.example: The prefix gathers everything into one.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把一切收进一个。

items.example: The root gives the turning towards one.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出「转向一」的意思。
它把 universus 变成 universal。

definition_zh: 宇宙；万物；领域；范围；全体
definition_en: all of space and everything in it, or a particular area of interest or activity
core_image: 无数星点在一个不断向外膨胀的巨大黑暗球体里旋转，全部合成一个整体
scene: 天文台的圆顶在夜里滑开，望远镜对准一片几乎看不见的星云。Astronomers say the universe is still expanding today.
sceneCN: 这里 universe 是「宇宙」（第 1 个义项：整个空间及其中的一切）；句意为天文学家说宇宙如今仍在膨胀。全部星点合为一体的那一整片，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 与本词同源，义为「普遍的；全体的」
由 universal 加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地」
与本词同源，义为「大学」，原指学者的全体
由 univers 加 -ology 与 -ical 构成，义为「宇宙学的」

senses.title: All of space and matter
senses.definition: all of space and everything in it, taken as one whole
senses.definitionCN: 整个空间及其中的一切，被视为一个整体
senses.example: Light from the farthest galaxies has travelled most of the age of the universe.
senses.exampleCN: 最远星系的光已经走了宇宙年龄的大部分时间。
senses.why: Unus is one and versus is turned: all things turned into a single whole.
senses.whyCN: unus 是「一」，versus 是「转」：万物转成一个整体。

senses.title: A field of activity
senses.definition: a particular area of knowledge, activity, or interest with its own laws
senses.definitionCN: 具有自身规律的一个特定知识、活动或兴趣领域
senses.example: In the universe of small business, cash flow is the first rule.
senses.exampleCN: 在小型企业的领域里，现金流是第一法则。
senses.why: A field so large that it has its own laws is felt to be a whole, and the name for the whole is applied to it.
senses.whyCN: 一个大到有自身法则的范围会被感觉成一个整体，而表示整体的名称就被用到它身上。

senses.title: The whole set of something
senses.definition: the complete collection of a kind of thing, without exception
senses.definitionCN: 某一类事物的完整集合，没有例外
senses.example: The survey tried to cover the universe of public libraries in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查试图覆盖全国公共图书馆的全体。
senses.why: Counting every member and stopping at nothing gives the same total that the word first meant.
senses.whyCN: 把每个成员都数上而不留下任何例外，得到的就是这个词最初所指的那个总和。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: a set of people with shared work or interests, such as the art world
senses.definitionCN: 因工作或兴趣相同而聚成的一群人，如艺术界
senses.example: Her paintings are well known inside the fashion universe.
senses.exampleCN: 她的画作在时尚圈里广为人知。
senses.why: People who share a trade form a closed circle, and a closed circle is a small universe of its own.
senses.whyCN: 同行的人形成一个封闭的圈子，而封闭的圈子本身就是一个小小的宇宙。

senses.title: A world of one's own
senses.definition: an imagined or invented world, as in a fictional or parallel universe
senses.definitionCN: 想象或虚构出来的世界，如小说世界或平行宇宙
senses.example: Every novel creates a small universe with its own weather and laws.
senses.exampleCN: 每部小说都创造出一个有自己的天气与法则的小世界。
senses.why: If a whole needs nothing outside itself, an invented one can be complete too, and the word is lent to fiction.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个整体无需外物即可自足，那么虚构的整体也可以完整，这个词便借给了小说。

intro.en: Universe comes straight from a Latin adjective meaning turned into one, and became a noun in French before English.
intro.cn: universe 直接来自一个意为「合成一个」的拉丁语形容词，在法语中先成为名词，再进入英语。

items.en: Unus meant one and vertere meant to turn; universus described many things turned into one whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，vertere 意为「转动」；universus 表示许多事物转成一个整体。

items.en: The neuter form universum was used as a noun for the whole of things.
items.cn: 其中性形式 universum 被用作名词，指万物的全体。

items.en: Old French univers took the noun for the totality of creation, and used it for a whole community as well.
items.cn: 古法语 univers 接纳了这个名词，指造物的全体，也用来指一个完整的团体。

items.en: English adopted universe for the whole of created things, earth and heavens together.
items.cn: 英语以 universe 指被造万物的全体，天地合在一起。

items.en: Astronomy redrew the word as all of space and time, and everyday speech borrowed it for any large field or circle.
items.cn: 天文学把这个词界定为整个空间与时间，日常言语又借它指任何大的领域或圈子。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same one-and-turn root; the near-meaning group gathers words for totalities of different kinds.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「合一」词根上的词；近义组收表示不同类型整体的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning true of everyone or everything.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「普遍的、全体的」。

entries.definition: A place of higher learning; once a whole guild of scholars.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大学」，原指学者的整个行会。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning by all or in every case.
The plural, used for imagined or parallel worlds.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，多用于虚构世界或平行宇宙。

entries.definition: Varied and unlike each other; it contains vers but no one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，含 vers 但不含「一」。

entries.definition: The universe seen as an ordered, harmonious whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宇宙」，强调其有秩序的和谐整体。

entries.definition: All that exists, seen as made by a creator.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「造物、万物」，带有被创造的含义。

entries.definition: The earth and its people, or a particular sphere of life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「世界」，也可指某个生活领域。

entries.definition: A kingdom or a distinct area of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「领域、王国」，指一个独立的范围。

entries.definition: One of the large systems of stars; only a part of the universe.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「星系」，只是宇宙的一部分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin pieces of the word and the phrases it appears in today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词的拉丁部件，以及它今天常见的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- is one and verse is turn: the whole of things turned into one.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，verse 是「转」：万物转成一个。

normal.en: The universe is still expanding, so the word names something it cannot hold still.
normal.cn: 宇宙仍在膨胀，因此这个词命名的东西无法静止。

normal.en: University carries the same root: one whole community of scholars.
normal.cn: university 有同一词根：一整个学者的团体。

normal.en: A parallel universe is invented; the fashion universe is merely a large circle.
normal.cn: 平行宇宙是虚构的；时尚界只是一大圈人。

normal.en: The universe of libraries means every library, counted together.
normal.cn: 图书馆的全体指把所有图书馆加在一起。

abstract.en: Picture every star turned towards one centre: the word started as an act of gathering, not a place.
abstract.cn: 想象所有星辰都朝向同一个中心：这个词起初是收拢的动作，而不是一个地点。

abstract.en: Any field large enough to have its own rules gets called a universe, because it is whole inside itself.
abstract.cn: 任何大到有自己规则的领域都会被称作一个宇宙，因为它在内部自成整体。

abstract.en: The word is an answer to a question: what is there, if you count everything at once.
abstract.cn: 这个词回答的是一个问题：如果把所有东西一次数完，那里有什么。

examples.en: Scientists still argue about how the universe began.
examples.cn: 科学家们仍在争论宇宙是如何开始的。

examples.en: In the universe of online shops, speed of delivery decides everything.
examples.cn: 在网络商店这个领域里，送货速度决定一切。

examples.en: The novel builds a universe where people can hear each other's thoughts.
examples.cn: 这部小说构建了一个人们能听见彼此心思的世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼沃斯」——优尼把沃斯整个转成一团：宇宙、全体

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」加 vertere「转动」构成的 universus「合成一个的、整个的」，其中性形式 universum 作名词指万物全体，经古法语 univers 进入英语，近代天文学用来指整个空间与时间。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of universe all name a whole gathered into one: all of space, a field with its own rules, a complete set, a circle of people, or an imagined world.
sensesIntro.cn: universe 的五个义项都在命名被收成一个的整体：整个空间、自成一体的领域、完整的集合、一圈人，或虚构的世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: countless stars turning inside one vast sphere of darkness.
core.cn: 核心意象：无数星点在同一个巨大黑暗球体里旋转。

branches.en: THE COSMOS: space and every object in it, taken together.
branches.cn: 宇宙线：空间及其中的每一个物体，合在一起。

branches.en: THE FIELD: one area of activity with its own rules.
branches.cn: 领域线：一个有自身规则的特定活动范围。

branches.en: THE SET: every member of a kind, without exception.
branches.cn: 集合线：某一类里的每个成员，没有例外。

branches.en: THE CIRCLE: a group of people who share a world.
branches.cn: 圈子线：共享同一个世界的一群人。

branches.en: THE INVENTION: fiction builds small universes of its own.
branches.cn: 虚构线：小说造出自己的一方小宇宙。

intro.en: Universe is a two-piece Latin compound, and the rest of its family is made with English suffixes.
intro.cn: universe 是两段组成的拉丁语复合词，家族其余成员由英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Unus, vertere and universus are all recorded, and universum appears as a noun in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus、vertere、universus 均有记录，universum 在拉丁语中作名词使用。

items.example: It closes the Latin adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁语形容词收成名词。

definition_zh: 卸货；卸下；退出子弹；倾诉（心事）；卸载（数据）
definition_en: to remove goods from a vehicle, to take bullets out of a gun, or to tell someone your worries
core_image: 卡车后挡板放下，几个工人把一箱箱货搬下来，车厢一点点变轻变空
scene: 货车在仓库门口倒车停稳，司机跳下来掀开帆布，晨光里全是灰尘。They began to unload the boxes at six in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 unload 是「卸货、卸下」（第 1 个义项：把货物从车船上搬走）；句意为他们早上六点开始卸箱子。车厢一点点被搬空的那种变轻感觉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 倾诉；把心里的负担说出来

collocations.zh: 向某人倾诉；把情绪发泄到某人身上

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「卸货；卸载」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「未装货的；未装弹的」
本词去掉 un-，义为「装载；装填」
由 load 加 -er 构成，义为「装卸工；装载机」

senses.title: Take goods off
senses.definition: to remove goods or cargo from a ship, truck, or other carrier
senses.definitionCN: 把货物从船、卡车等运输工具上搬下来
senses.example: The crew unloaded the fish onto the wet harbour stones.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们把鱼卸到湿漉漉的码头石板上。
senses.why: Un- reverses and load is what was put on board: the cargo comes off, and the ship rides higher.
senses.whyCN: un- 表示反向，load 是被装上的东西：货物离船，船身也随之抬高。

senses.title: Take the bullets out
senses.definition: to remove the ammunition from a gun so that it cannot fire
senses.definitionCN: 把弹药从枪里取出，使枪不能击发
senses.example: He unloaded the rifle before handing it to the guide.
senses.exampleCN: 他把步枪里的子弹退出来，才交给向导。
senses.why: A gun is loaded like a cart, so the same verb empties it and makes it safe to pass on.
senses.whyCN: 枪和车一样会被「装上」东西，因此同一个动词让它变空、变得可以递出去。

senses.title: Put down a burden
senses.definition: to set down something heavy that one has been carrying
senses.definitionCN: 把一直扛着的重物放下来
senses.example: The porters unloaded their baskets at the top of the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 搬运工在台阶顶上把筐放下。
senses.why: Here the carrier is a person, and the load is carried on the back rather than in a vehicle.
senses.whyCN: 这里的载具是人，负载扛在背上而不是装在车里。

senses.title: Tell someone your worries
senses.titleCN: 倾诉；把心里的话说出来
senses.definition: in informal speech, to tell someone all your problems or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中，把烦恼或感受全部说给别人听
senses.example: She called her sister to unload after the long meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开完那个长会，她打电话给姐姐倾诉了一番。
senses.why: Trouble behaves like freight: once it is set down on someone else, the speaker feels lighter.
senses.whyCN: 烦恼像货物一样：一旦放到别人那边，说话的人就轻了。

senses.title: Remove from a system
senses.definition: of data or software, to transfer it out or remove it from a place
senses.definitionCN: 指数据或程序，把它们转移出去或从某处移除
senses.example: The app unloads the photos to save space on the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用把照片卸载出去，以节省手机空间。
senses.why: A phone or a server is the new warehouse, and its files are the freight to be moved out.
senses.whyCN: 手机或服务器成了新的仓库，里面的文件就是待搬出的货。

intro.en: Unload is the native negative prefix on load, a word that English took from the same Germanic root as lade.
intro.cn: unload 是本土否定前缀加 load，load 与 lade 同出日耳曼语词根，为英语所继承。

items.en: The verb hladan meant to draw water or to pile up goods, and gave the modern lade and load.
items.cn: 古英语动词 hladan 意为「舀水、堆货」，演变为现代的 lade 与 load。

items.en: The noun lode, meaning a load or a course, and the verb laden kept the sense of piling a burden on.
items.cn: 中古英语名词 lode 意为「负载、路线」，动词 laden 保留了「堆积重负」之意。

items.en: Un- was added to make unload, to take the burden off again, and the word covered ships, carts and guns.
items.cn: 加上 un- 构成 unload，表示把重负重新取下，用于船、车与枪。

items.en: Railways and lorries made unloading a daily industrial routine, with dockside cranes named for it.
items.cn: 铁路与卡车让卸货成为日常的工业工序，码头的吊机也以它命名。

items.en: Computers and counselling both borrowed the image: data and worries can now be unloaded too.
items.cn: 计算机与心理咨询都借用了这个意象：数据与心事如今也能「卸」出去。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words in un- and load forms; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of removing, emptying, or confessing.
note.cn: 形近组收 un- 与 load 一族的词；近义组收表示移走、清空或倾诉的动词。

entries.definition: To put goods or ammunition on; the word without the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装载」，即去掉前缀的词。

entries.definition: Adjective for a vehicle or gun with nothing in it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未装货的、未装弹的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the work of taking a load off.
To send data from a computer to a server; the opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上传」，方向相反。

entries.definition: To bring data from a network onto a device.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「下载」，从网络取到设备上。

entries.definition: To make a container have nothing in it; the result rather than the work.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「倒空」，强调结果。

entries.definition: To unload cargo formally, or to release a person; used in shipping and law.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「卸货、释放」，多用于航运与法律。

entries.definition: To relieve oneself of a worry by telling someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「卸下负担、倾诉」，偏书面。

entries.definition: To tell a secret to someone you trust; quieter than unload.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吐露」，比 unload 更安静、更私密。

entries.definition: A general verb for taking something away from a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「移走」，泛称从某处拿走东西。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain un- plus load structure and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 un 加 load 的朴素结构，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Un- means not and load is the burden: unload is to take the burden off.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，load 是重负：unload 就是把重负取下。

normal.en: A truck is unloaded at the dock; a gun is unloaded before it is handed over.
normal.cn: 卡车在码头卸货；枪在交出之前要退出子弹。

normal.en: Upload and download move data; unload moves it out of the way.
normal.cn: upload 与 download 是搬数据；unload 是把数据挪走。

normal.en: To unload on someone can mean to tell them your troubles, or to blame them.
normal.cn: unload on someone 既可指向人倾诉，也可指把气撒到人身上。

normal.en: Unloaded and empty are close, but unload is the act.
normal.cn: unloaded 与 empty 意思接近，但 unload 是动作。

abstract.en: Picture a cart that gets lighter with every box: the word tracks the moment weight leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车每卸一箱就轻一点：这个词跟着重量离开的那一瞬间。

abstract.en: From boxes to bullets to worries, unload always means the same: take the charge out.
abstract.cn: 从货物到子弹再到心事，unload 始终是同一个意思：把「装进去的东西」拿出来。

abstract.en: A person who unloads a burden is the same image, only the cargo cannot be seen.
abstract.cn: 倾诉的人用的是同一个意象，只是货物看不见。

examples.en: Workers unloaded the truck in less than an hour.
examples.cn: 工人们不到一小时就把卡车卸完了。

examples.en: Always unload the gun before cleaning it.
examples.cn: 清洁枪支前一定要先退出子弹。

examples.en: She unloaded her worries onto her friend over dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭时她把心里的烦恼全向朋友倾诉了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的楼德」——安把楼上堆的货物一件件搬下来：卸货

root: 由否定前缀 un- 加 load（源自古英语 hladan「舀水、堆货」，与 lade 同源）构成，字面即「把装上的东西取下」；近代从船只、车辆、枪械扩展到数据与心事的「卸载」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unload all remove a charge that had been put in: goods, bullets, a heavy basket, pent-up worries, or data.
sensesIntro.cn: unload 的五个义项都在把先前装进去的东西拿出来：货物、子弹、重筐、憋着的心事，或数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the tailgate drops and boxes are carried out of the truck.
core.cn: 核心意象：后挡板放下，箱子一箱箱被搬出车厢。

branches.en: THE CARGO: goods leave the ship, truck or plane.
branches.cn: 货物线：货物离开船、卡车或飞机。

branches.en: THE AMMUNITION: bullets leave the gun so it is safe.
branches.cn: 弹药线：子弹离开枪膛，枪才安全。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: a carried basket is set down at the top of the steps.
branches.cn: 重负线：扛着的筐在台阶顶上被放下。

branches.en: THE FEELINGS: what was held inside is said out loud.
branches.cn: 情感线：憋在里面的东西被说出口。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: data is moved out to free space.
branches.cn: 系统线：数据被移出去以腾出空间。

intro.en: Unload is native on both sides: an English prefix on an English verb, with English suffixes on top.
intro.cn: unload 两边都是本土成分：英语前缀加英语动词，上面再加英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin core here; the Latin-based cousins appear only as formal near meanings.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语核心；拉丁语来源的近义词只作为正式说法列出。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「装载」倒过来。

items.example: The root names the charge being carried.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被装上的负载。
它把 load 变成 loader。

items.example: An older noun from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根上较早的名词。

items.example: The formal synonym from Latin carricare.
items.exampleCN: 源自拉丁语 carricare 的正式近义词。

definition_zh: 前所未有的；史无前例的；空前的；无先例可循的
definition_en: never having happened, existed or been done before, so that no earlier case exists to serve as a guide
core_image: 档案柜里一排旧水位刻线都很低，今年的水痕却高过所有旧线，旁边的人仰头看着新刻痕
scene: 气象站的老档案里，过去一百年的最高水位都低于今年的刻线，工作人员围着新水痕拍照。The flood reached an unprecedented level last week.
sceneCN: 这里指水位达到从未有过的高度（第 1 个义项：规模或程度前所未有）；句意为上周洪水达到了前所未有的水位。图中可辨识物件：旧档案柜、一排低刻线、高过所有旧线的新水痕、拍照的工作人员。

pos.zh: 前所未有的；史无前例的；空前的

derivatives.zh: 由前缀加「行走」词根构成的名词，义为「先例；在前的」
同一词根的基础动词，义为「先于；走在前面」
由动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「在前的」
由词干加表示次序的名词词尾构成，义为「优先；优先权」
由本词加副词词尾构成，义为「前所未有地」

senses.title: A scale never reached before
senses.definition: existing at a size or intensity for which no earlier example can be found
senses.definitionCN: 达到一个找不到先前例子的规模或强度
senses.example: The flood reached an unprecedented level last week.
senses.exampleCN: 上周洪水达到了前所未有的水位。
senses.why: The negative prefix removes the earlier case, and the root supplies the walking that came before.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀去掉了「先前的例子」，词根则提供了「走在前面」的动作。

senses.title: An event with no earlier occurrence
senses.definition: an occurrence that has no previous instance in the record
senses.definitionCN: 在记录中找不到先前实例的事件
senses.example: The resignation was an unprecedented event in the company's history.
senses.exampleCN: 这次辞职在公司历史上是史无前例的事件。
senses.why: The word points to the record book: nothing on the earlier pages matches this page.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指向记录簿：前面几页没有任何内容与此页相符。

senses.title: A speed never seen before
senses.definition: a rate of change faster than any earlier measured rate
senses.definitionCN: 变化速度超过此前任何可测的速率
senses.example: The city grew at an unprecedented speed during those five years.
senses.exampleCN: 那五年里，这座城市以未曾有过的速度扩张。
senses.why: Speed is the dimension most often called unprecedented, because records measure it precisely.
senses.whyCN: 速度是这个词最常修饰的维度，因为记录能精确测量它。

senses.title: Demand or growth beyond all past peaks
senses.definition: a level of demand, growth or pressure higher than every earlier peak
senses.definitionCN: 需求、增长或压力高于此前每一个峰值
senses.example: The port handled unprecedented demand after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，港口承接了空前的需求。
senses.why: Economists use the word when a curve passes every earlier peak on the chart.
senses.whyCN: 当曲线越过图表上此前每一个峰值，经济学家就用这个词。

senses.title: A ruling with no legal precedent
senses.definition: a decision for which earlier courts or rules provide no model
senses.definitionCN: 此前的判例或规则无法提供范本的裁决
senses.example: The tribunal issued an unprecedented ruling on digital ownership.
senses.exampleCN: 该法庭就数字财产所有权作出了无先例可循的裁决。
senses.why: Law is built on precedent, so a case without one is formally exceptional.
senses.whyCN: 法律建立在先例之上，因此没有先例的案件在形式上就是例外。

senses.title: A rare and extreme natural event
senses.definition: a weather or natural event outside every earlier record for the place
senses.definitionCN: 超出一个地方此前全部记录的天气或自然事件
senses.example: Forecasters called the drought unprecedented for the region.
senses.exampleCN: 预报员称这场干旱是该地区前所未有的。
senses.why: Weather records are long and numeric, which makes the claim testable.
senses.whyCN: 气象记录漫长且数字化，因此这一说法可以被检验。

senses.title: A record-breaking performance
senses.definition: a result that surpasses every previous mark in a sport or field
senses.definitionCN: 超过某项运动或领域此前所有标记的成绩
senses.example: Her unprecedented run broke three national records.
senses.exampleCN: 她前所未有的这一跑打破了三项全国纪录。
senses.why: Sport gives the word a stopwatch and a scoreboard, where being first is measurable.
senses.whyCN: 体育给了这个词一块秒表和一块记分牌，在那里「第一次」是可以测量的。

senses.title: A break with established practice
senses.definition: an action that departs from the usual custom or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 偏离通常惯例或程序的行为
senses.example: The mayor took the unprecedented step of publishing the budget draft.
senses.exampleCN: 市长采取了公布预算草案这一打破常规的做法。
senses.why: Custom, not nature, is the baseline here; the new move has simply never been tried.
senses.whyCN: 这里的基线是惯例而非自然；这一新做法只是从未被尝试过。

senses.title: Something a person has never experienced
senses.definition: an experience outside the whole range of one person's earlier life
senses.definitionCN: 超出一个人此前全部生活范围的经历
senses.example: For the young teacher, the attention was unprecedented.
senses.exampleCN: 对这位年轻教师来说，这样的关注是前所未有的。
senses.why: The record can be personal as well as public: a single life also has earlier pages.
senses.whyCN: 记录既可以是公共的，也可以是个人的：一个人的生活同样有前面的页。

intro.en: Unprecedented is a negative prefix laid over a Latin verb for going before: no earlier case has gone ahead to show the way.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个否定前缀加在一个表示「走在前面」的拉丁动词上：没有先前的例子先走过、指出道路。

items.en: cedere meant to go, to yield, to move along; it is the walking root inside the word.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让、前行」，是这个词内部的「行走」词根。

items.en: prae- meant before, so praecedere was to go before someone or something.
items.cn: prae- 表示「在前」，因此 praecedere 意为「走在某人或某物前面」。

items.en: The participle praecedens described what comes first, and English took it as precedent.
items.cn: 分词 praecedens 描述先出现的事物，英语把它借作 precedent。

items.en: A precedent is an earlier case used as a model; the word settled into law and general usage.
items.cn: 先例是被当作范本的先前案例；这个词在法律与一般用法中固定下来。

items.en: The negative prefix denies the existence of such a model, and the adjective ending attaches it to the case at hand.
items.cn: 否定前缀否认存在这样的范本，形容词词尾把它挂到眼前的案件上。

items.en: Statistics, journalism and sport made the adjective a standard way to say that the record book has no matching page.
items.cn: 统计、新闻与体育让这个形容词成为「记录簿里没有相符的一页」的标准说法。

note.en: The first group shares the going-before root or form; the second group names nearby ideas of being beyond all earlier examples.
note.cn: 第一组共享「走在前面」的词根或形音；第二组是与「超出此前所有例子」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: An earlier case or decision used as a guide; the noun that the negative adjective denies.
entries.definitionCN: 指被当作指南的先前案例或裁决；正是这个否定形容词所否认的名词。

entries.definition: To come or go before something else in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 指在时间或顺序上先于某物。

entries.definition: The right to go first, or priority in rank or order.
entries.definitionCN: 指优先前行的权利，或地位、次序上的优先。

entries.definition: In a manner that has never occurred before.
Free from bias; it looks close but its root is judging in advance, not going before.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有偏见的；形近，但其词根是「预先判断」，而非「走在前面」。

entries.definition: Having no equal in quality or degree; it stresses unmatched rank rather than a missing earlier case.
entries.definitionCN: 指质量或程度上无可匹敌；强调无与伦比，而非缺少先例。

entries.definition: Surpassing a measured mark; it is narrower and always tied to a recorded figure.
entries.definitionCN: 指超过某个已测标记；范围更窄，且总与记录数字相连。

entries.definition: New and original; it stresses freshness rather than the absence of any earlier instance.
entries.definitionCN: 指新颖独创；强调新鲜，而非完全没有先前实例。

entries.definition: Being the only one of its kind; it stresses singularity, not historical record.
entries.definitionCN: 指同类中唯一；强调独一无二，而非历史记录。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin go-before image, the real legal idea of precedent, and the real record phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「走在前面」意象、真实的法律先例概念，以及真实的记录搭配。

normal.en: pre- means before and cedere means go: a precedent is a case that walked ahead of you.
normal.cn: pre- 是「在前」，cedere 是「走」：先例就是走在你前面的案例。

normal.en: Add un- and no case has walked ahead; the road has never been walked.
normal.cn: 加上 un-，就没有案例走在前头；这条路从未有人走过。

normal.en: Unprecedented scale, unprecedented demand and unprecedented event are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 空前的规模、空前的需求与史无前例的事件是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Law lives on precedent, so a case without one is professionally shocking.
normal.cn: 法律靠先例生活，因此没有先例的案件在专业上令人震动。

normal.en: The word says nothing about quality, only about the empty earlier pages.
normal.cn: 这个词不评价好坏，只说前面的页是空的。

abstract.en: A record book is a promise that the future will resemble the past; this word announces that it did not.
abstract.cn: 记录簿是一份「未来会像过去」的承诺；这个词宣布它没有兑现。

abstract.en: Unprecedented does not mean better, only unmatched; the first of anything can be the worst.
abstract.cn: 前所未有并不意味着更好，只意味着无从比对；任何「第一次」都可能是最糟的一次。

abstract.en: Every unprecedented event becomes a precedent the moment it is written down.
abstract.cn: 每一个史无前例的事件，在被写下的那一刻就成了先例。

examples.en: The city is preparing for an unprecedented number of visitors this summer.
examples.cn: 这座城市正在为今夏前所未有的游客数量做准备。

examples.en: Scientists described the collapse of the ice shelf as unprecedented in the satellite record.
examples.cn: 科学家称冰架的崩塌在卫星记录中前所未有。

examples.en: The committee took the unprecedented step of reopening the hearing.
examples.cn: 委员会采取了重新开启听证会这一史无前例的举动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安普瑞西登提德」——前面没有任何「先例」走过

root: 由否定前缀 un- + precedent + 形容词词尾 -ed 构成；precedent 来自拉丁语 praecedere「走在前面」← prae-「在前」+ cedere「走、让」，分词 praecedens。词源链清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a scale and an event with no earlier case through speed, demand, law, weather, sport and custom to one person's private experience.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从没有先前例子的规模与事件，经过速度、需求、法律、天气、体育与惯例，最后落到一个人的私人经历。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of old marks on a wall all sit low, and the new water stain rises above every one.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上旧刻线都低低一排，新水痕却高过其中每一条。

branches.en: THE FIRST PAGE: a scale and an event for which the record book is blank.
branches.cn: 第一页：规模与事件在记录簿上都是空白。

branches.en: THE FAST CURVE: speed and demand that pass every earlier peak.
branches.cn: 陡峭曲线：速度与需求越过此前每个峰值。

branches.en: THE EMPTY CASE LAW: a ruling with no earlier court to follow.
branches.cn: 空白判例：裁决没有先前的法庭可循。

branches.en: THE EXTREME MARK: weather beyond the archive and a score beyond the board.
branches.cn: 极端标记：天气超出档案，成绩超出记分牌。

branches.en: THE UNTRIED MOVE: a custom broken and a life that has never met this before.
branches.cn: 未试之举：被打破的惯例，以及一个人从未遇到过的经历。

intro.en: Unprecedented is a negative prefix, a prefix meaning before, a walking root and an adjective ending stacked in one word.
intro.cn: 这个词把否定前缀、表「在前」的前缀、「行走」词根与形容词词尾叠在一个词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies cedere and praecedere; English adds precedent, then un- and -ed to deny any earlier model.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 cedere 与 praecedere；英语先构成 precedent，再加 un- 与 -ed 否认任何先前范本。

items.example: It denies the existence of the earlier case.
items.exampleCN: 它否认先前案例的存在。

items.example: It sets the direction of the walking.
Prefix and root form the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: It becomes the English noun precedent.
The noun is what un- denies.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词正是 un- 所否认的。

items.example: It turns the noun into the adjective.
The verb keeps the walking image.
The noun of rank uses the same root.
items.exampleCN: 表次序的名词使用同一词根。

definition_zh: 上面的；较高的；上部的；上游的；上层的；（地位）较高的
definition_en: higher in position or rank than something else
core_image: 两层抽屉，上面那层要抬手才够得着
scene: 书架从地面一直顶到天花板，最上面那几排书要搬梯子才拿得到。The upper shelves are full of old magazines.
sceneCN: 这里 upper 是「上面的」（第 1 个义项：位置较高的）；句意为上面几层书架塞满了旧杂志。抬手才够得着的上层抽屉，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 由 upper 加 -most 构成，义为「最高的；最上面的」
upper 的比较级词尾所由来的原副词，义为「向上」
由 up 加 -wards 构成，义为「向上；朝上」

senses.title: Higher of two parts
senses.definition: higher in position when two parts are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较两部分时位置较高的那一部分
senses.example: The upper drawer holds the knives.
senses.exampleCN: 上面那层抽屉放的是刀。
senses.why: The word is the old comparative of up, so it simply means the more up of two things.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 up 较古老的比较级，字面就是「两者中更靠上的那个」。

senses.title: Near the top of a building or body
senses.definition: used of the part of a building or a body nearer the top
senses.definitionCN: 形容建筑或身体靠近顶端的部分
senses.example: He lives on the upper floor of the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在这栋老房子的楼上。
senses.why: A building is vertical, so the part nearer the roof is literally the more up part.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是竖着的，因此靠近屋顶的那部分字面上就是「更靠上的一端」。

senses.title: Higher in rank or class
senses.definition: used of people of higher social or official rank
senses.definitionCN: 形容社会或职务等级较高的人
senses.example: The upper class lived behind the park.
senses.exampleCN: 上层人家住在公园后面。
senses.why: Social rank is pictured as height, and the higher people are said to be in, the more the word applies.
senses.whyCN: 社会等级被画成了高度，人所在的位置越「高」，这个词就用得越贴切。

senses.title: Further up a river
senses.definition: used of the part of a river further from the sea
senses.definitionCN: 形容河流离海较远的一段
senses.example: They swam in the upper reaches of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河的上游河段游泳。
senses.why: A river runs downhill, so the higher part of the land gives the upper part of the stream.
senses.whyCN: 河往低处流，因此地势较高的那一段就成了溪流的上游。

senses.title: The higher of two limits
senses.definition: used of the highest figure allowed or recorded
senses.definitionCN: 形容允许或记录的最高数值
senses.example: The upper limit for the room is twenty people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间的上限是二十人。
senses.why: Two bounds are compared exactly as two shelves are, and the higher one takes the word.
senses.whyCN: 两条界限的比较与两层架子的比较完全一样，较高的那条就用这个词。

senses.title: The top of a shoe
senses.definition: the part of a shoe above the sole
senses.definitionCN: 鞋底以上的部分
senses.example: The uppers are leather, the soles are rubber.
senses.exampleCN: 鞋帮是皮的，鞋底是橡胶的。
senses.why: The part of a shoe that rises above the sole is named by the same word that means the higher of two.
senses.whyCN: 鞋底之上升高起来的那部分，用的仍是表示「较高者」的这个词。

intro.en: The old comparative of up, kept as a separate adjective while the verb moved on.
intro.cn: up 的古老比较级形式，在其他用法继续演变时被保留为独立形容词。

items.en: The root upp means up, and a comparative form existed early in the family.
items.cn: 词根 upp 意为「向上」，这一语族很早就有了比较级形式。

items.en: The word yferra served as the comparative of up and meant higher.
items.cn: 古英语 yferra 充当 up 的比较级，意为「更高的」。

items.en: The form develops into upper, while up remains an adverb and particle.
items.cn: 这一形式后来发展为 upper，而 up 保持副词与小品词的身份。

items.en: Upper takes on social meaning in upper class and upper house.
items.cn: upper 在 upper class、upper house 中获得社会与制度义。

items.en: Concrete uses such as shoe uppers and upper limit keep the word physical.
items.cn: upper 也用于鞋帮、上限这类具体说法，保持着实感。

note.en: The look-alike group collects up- words and their compounds, while the near-meaning group compares words for height and rank.
note.cn: 形近组收集 up 系词及其复合词，近义组比较表示高低与等级的词。

normalIntro.en: One of the few words in English that preserves an old comparative ending outside the usual two-tier pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 英语中少数保留了古老比较级词尾、却不属于通常两级体系的词之一。

normal.en: Upper is the comparison of up, not of a simple adjective.
normal.cn: upper 是 up 的比较形式，并非普通形容词的比较级。

normal.en: The upper hand comes from an old game and now means an advantage.
normal.cn: the upper hand 源自一种古老游戏，现在指占上风。

normal.en: Upper class and upper house are the social and political uses.
normal.cn: upper class 与 upper house 是它的社会与政治用法。

normal.en: Uppermost adds -most for the very top.
normal.cn: uppermost 加 -most 表示最顶端。

normal.en: Shoe uppers are the part above the sole.
normal.cn: shoe uppers 指鞋底以上的那部分。

abstract.en: Reach up for the drawer above your head.
abstract.cn: 伸手去够头顶上方的抽屉。

abstract.en: See two shelves and only the high one is full.
abstract.cn: 看见两层架子，只有上面那层是满的。

abstract.en: Follow a river upstream until the boats stop.
abstract.cn: 顺着河往上游走，直到不见船。

examples.en: The books on the upper shelf are covered with dust.
examples.cn: 上层架子上的书落了灰尘。

examples.en: After two hours she had the upper hand in the argument.
examples.cn: 两小时后，她在争论中占了上风。

examples.en: The town lies on the upper course of the river.
examples.cn: 这个镇位于河流的上游段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆」——阿婆伸手去够柜子最上层那格，够不着就搬来凳子。

root: 古英语 yferra，为 up 的比较级形式，源自日耳曼语词根 upp（向上）；中古英语演变为 upper

sensesIntro.en: One comparison, the more up of two, moves from furniture to buildings, ranks, rivers, limits, and shoes.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个比较「两者中更靠上的」，从家具走到建筑、等级、河流、上限与鞋帮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for the higher of two drawers.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手去够两层抽屉里更上面的那层。

branches.en: The comparison branch: two parts, the higher one.
branches.cn: 比较分支：两部分中较高的那部分。

branches.en: The building branch: floors near the roof.
branches.cn: 建筑分支：靠近屋顶的楼层。

branches.en: The rank branch: people who sit higher in society.
branches.cn: 等级分支：在社会中位置更高的人。

branches.en: The river branch: the part nearer the source.
branches.cn: 河流分支：靠近源头的一段。

branches.en: The limit and shoe branches: a ceiling figure, a shoe top.
branches.cn: 上限与鞋帮分支：封顶的数字、鞋的上部。

intro.en: A comparative form of an old adverb, now working as an adjective in fixed pairs.
intro.cn: 一个古老副词的比较级形式，如今作形容词用于固定搭配。

latinIntro.en: Latin marks higher comparison with the suffix -ior, as in superior and inferus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用词尾 -ior 表示较高比较，如 superior 与 inferus。

items.exampleCN: up 加了更古老的比较级词尾。

items.example: The upper limit is ten litres.

definition_zh: 直立的；竖立的；正直的；诚实的；立式（钢琴）
definition_en: standing straight up, or honest and of good character
core_image: 一根木杆笔直地立在雪地里
scene: 雪后的院子里，晾衣杆笔直插着，风吹也没倾斜。The old post stood upright in the snow.
sceneCN: 这里 upright 是「立着的」（第 1 个义项：竖直、不歪）；句意为那根旧木杆直直地立在雪里。木杆笔直立着的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「正直地；笔直地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「正直；直立」
复合词的前一部分，义为「向上」
复合词的后一部分，义为「直的；正当的」

senses.title: Standing straight up
senses.definition: positioned vertically, with the top directly above the base
senses.definitionCN: 顶端正对底端的竖直摆放
senses.example: He put the box upright against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他把箱子竖着靠在墙边。
senses.why: The compound joins up and right in its old sense of straight, so upright means standing straight up.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词由 up 与 right（古义「直的」）合起来，意思就是「笔直地立着」。

senses.title: Sitting or standing with a straight back
senses.definition: used of a person whose back is straight and not bent
senses.definitionCN: 形容人背脊挺直不弯
senses.example: She sat upright throughout the whole interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面试过程中她都坐得笔直。
senses.why: A spine held straight is the body applying the vertical line of a standing post.
senses.whyCN: 把脊背挺直，就是身体在实践一根立杆的垂直线。

senses.title: Honest in character
senses.definition: used of people who follow what is right and fair
senses.definitionCN: 形容按是非公道行事的人
senses.example: He was an upright man who never took a bribe.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个从不受贿的正直人。
senses.why: The picture of a body that does not bend yields the moral sense: a character that does not lean either.
senses.whyCN: 身体不弯的画面生出道德义：品行也不肯向哪一边歪。

senses.title: Not lying on its side
senses.definition: used of objects stored or carried vertically
senses.definitionCN: 形容竖着存放或搬运的物件
senses.example: Keep the bottles upright in the box.
senses.exampleCN: 把瓶子竖着放进箱子里。
senses.why: An object placed on its base instead of its side repeats the core picture exactly.
senses.whyCN: 把物件立在底座上而不是横躺着，正是核心画面的直接复现。

senses.title: A piano with vertical strings
senses.definition: a piano whose strings run vertically
senses.definitionCN: 琴弦竖直排列的钢琴
senses.example: An upright piano fits into a small room.
senses.exampleCN: 立式钢琴能放进小房间。
senses.why: The word names the instrument by the direction in which it stands, as opposed to the long grand.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是按其竖立的方向来给这种琴命名的，以区别于横卧的三角钢琴。

intro.en: An English compound of two native words, one of direction and one of straightness.
intro.cn: 一个由两个本土词合成的英语复合词，一个表方向，一个表笔直。

items.en: Up is an old adverb of upward motion, and riht meant straight or just.
items.cn: up 是表示向上的古副词，riht 意为「直的、正当的」。

items.en: The idea of standing riht, straight, already carried a moral tone.
items.cn: 「站得正」的说法在当时就已带有道德意味。

items.en: The compound upright appears and describes posts and persons alike.
items.cn: 复合词 upright 出现，既形容木杆也形容人。

items.en: The moral sense widens through upright citizen and upright judge.
items.cn: 道德义经由 upright citizen、upright judge 这样的说法扩展开来。

items.en: The noun use names things that stand straight, above all the upright piano.
items.cn: 名词用法指竖立之物，其中最突出的是立式钢琴。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers up- and right-based compounds, while the near-meaning group compares vertical words and words of honesty.
note.cn: 形近组汇集以 up 与 right 为基础的复合词，近义组比较竖直与诚实的词。

entries.definition: correct or straight
higher
entries.definitionCN: 上面的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: towards the top
morally right
going straight up
not bent
telling the truth
bent or dishonest

normalIntro.en: A picture word made of two very old parts, one of them carrying a moral sense from the start.
normalIntro.cn: 一个画面感很强的词，由两个极古老的部件构成，其中一个从一开始就带道德意味。

normal.en: Up plus right: right here means straight, not correct.
normal.cn: up 加 right：这里的 right 指「直」，不是「对」。

normal.en: Sit upright and stand upright keep the physical picture.
normal.cn: sit upright 与 stand upright 保持身体画面。

normal.en: Upright citizen and upright judge carry the moral sense.
normal.cn: upright citizen 与 upright judge 承载道德义。

normal.en: An upright piano stands straight against a wall.
normal.cn: 立式钢琴直立着靠墙摆放。

normal.en: The noun is uprightness, the adverb uprightly.
normal.cn: 名词是 uprightness，副词是 uprightly。

abstract.en: See a post standing straight in fresh snow.
abstract.cn: 想象一根木杆在新雪里笔直立着。

abstract.en: Feel a spine that will not bend under weight.
abstract.cn: 体会一根在重压下不肯弯的脊背。

abstract.en: Watch a lamp shade put back on its base.
abstract.cn: 看灯罩被重新正正地安回底座。

examples.en: Please keep the crate upright while you carry it.
examples.cn: 搬这个木箱时请保持直立。

examples.en: The children sat upright as the teacher came in.
examples.cn: 老师进来时，孩子们坐得笔直。

examples.en: He was known as an upright official who took nothing.
examples.cn: 他出名的是做官正直，分文不取。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普莱特」——阿普把木杆竖起来插在院子里，立得直直的，怎么也扳不歪。

root: 英语复合词：up（向上）+ right（直的、正当的），right 在此取其古老义「笔直的」，与拉丁语 rectus 同源，故本义为「笔直立着」

sensesIntro.en: One straight line from base to top gives the posture, then the honest character, then the standing object.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条从底到顶的直线先给姿势，再给正直品性，最后给竖立之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a post standing dead straight in snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根在雪里笔直立着的木杆。

branches.en: The position branch: top directly over base.
branches.cn: 位置分支：顶端正对底端。

branches.en: The posture branch: a back that does not bend.
branches.cn: 姿势分支：不肯弯的脊背。

branches.en: The character branch: a person who does not lean.
branches.cn: 品性分支：不肯偏向一边的人。

branches.en: The storage branch: boxes and crates set on end.
branches.cn: 存放分支：竖着安放的箱与板。

branches.en: The object branch: a piano with strings standing up.
branches.cn: 物件分支：琴弦竖立的钢琴。

intro.en: Two native words in a compound, and the second one keeps its old sense of straight.
intro.cn: 两个本土词构成的复合词，后一个保留了「直」的旧义。

latinIntro.en: The same idea appears in Latin rectus, straight, the source of upright and of erect.
latinIntro.cn: 同一概念见于拉丁语 rectus（直的），它也是 upright 与 erect 这类概念的来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 他给出了一个正直的回答。

definition_zh: 打翻；弄翻；使心烦；使不适；（比赛）意外击败；心烦的；不快的
definition_en: to knock something over, to make someone unhappy, or to beat a stronger opponent unexpectedly
core_image: 手肘一碰，杯子朝桌上倒下去
scene: 婚礼前夜，有人把饮料碰洒在新娘的礼服上，所有人都慌了。The news upset her so much that she could not sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 upset 是「使心烦」（第 2 个义项：让人心里翻腾不快）；句意为这个消息让她心烦得整夜没睡。手肘碰倒杯子的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 来自 distress 的过去分词，义为「痛苦的；忧虑的」
由 upset 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人不安的」

senses.title: To knock something over
senses.definition: to make a container or object fall over
senses.definitionCN: 使容器或物体倒下
senses.example: She upset the glass with her elbow.
senses.exampleCN: 她的手肘把杯子碰倒了。
senses.why: The word is up plus set: to set something up, or rather out of its place, until it falls over.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 up 加 set：把东西从原位「顶起来」，直到翻倒。

senses.title: To make someone unhappy
senses.definition: to make a person worried, hurt, or unhappy
senses.definitionCN: 使人担忧、难受或不快
senses.example: The letter upset him more than he showed.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让他心烦，比他表现出来的还要厉害。
senses.why: When a mind is knocked off balance like a cup, the person is upset, and the object becomes the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当心意像杯子一样被弄得失去平衡，人就成了 upset，物象便化为情绪。

senses.title: To disturb a plan or a system
senses.definition: to disturb an arrangement or a process
senses.definitionCN: 扰乱某个安排或进程
senses.example: The storm upset the whole timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨打乱了整个时刻表。
senses.why: A plan laid out like objects on a table can be knocked over too, and then nothing stays in place.
senses.whyCN: 摆好的计划就像桌上的物件，也可能被撞翻，之后便没有一样东西待在原位。

senses.title: To beat a stronger opponent
senses.definition: to defeat a team or player expected to win
senses.definitionCN: 击败被判为会赢的一方
senses.example: The visitors upset the champions in the final minute.
senses.exampleCN: 客队在最后一分钟爆冷赢下卫冕冠军。
senses.why: The result turns the table over: the side everyone placed first falls out of its place.
senses.whyCN: 这个结果把牌桌翻了过来：大家早先摆好的那一方从位子上跌落。

senses.title: A disturbed stomach
senses.definition: used of a stomach that feels unsettled
senses.definitionCN: 形容肚子不舒服、翻搅
senses.example: Too much fried food gives him an upset stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 油炸吃得太多，他就肠胃不适。
senses.why: Inside the body the same upsetting happens, and the stomach is described as turned over.
senses.whyCN: 身体内部也发生同样的翻搅，于是肠胃被说成「倒了」。

senses.title: A surprising defeat
senses.definition: a result in which the expected winner loses
senses.definitionCN: 本该获胜的一方却输了的结果
senses.example: The final was a real upset for the home crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛对主场观众来说是个大冷门。
senses.why: The noun keeps the picture of a table turned over, now applied to an expected result.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了桌面被翻掉的画面，只是这一次用在了原本意料之中的结果上。

intro.en: A two-part compound of native words whose first sense is physical and whose later senses are emotional.
intro.cn: 一个由本土词构成的两部分复合词，最初的意思是身体的，后来的意思是情绪的。

items.en: Up is an old adverb, and settan meant to place or put.
items.cn: up 是古副词，settan 意为「放置」。

items.en: Upsetten means to set up or to overturn, and the two meanings coexist.
items.cn: upsetten 兼有「竖起」与「推翻」两种意思，二者并存。

items.en: The sense of overturning settles first in the physical world of cups and carts.
items.cn: 「打翻」的意思先固定下来，用于杯子和推车这类实物。

items.en: By the eighteenth century upset describes a disturbed mind and a disturbed stomach.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，upset 已用于形容被搅乱的心情与肠胃。

items.en: The sports sense of an unexpected defeat appears in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「爆冷」这一体育含义在十九世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers up-set compounds and similar forms, while the near-meaning group collects words for troubling someone.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 up 与 set 组成的复合词及相近形式，近义组汇集表示使人难过的词。

the place or conditions around

normalIntro.en: A compound image that moves by easy steps from a falling cup to a troubled mind.
normalIntro.cn: 一个复合意象，从翻倒的杯子很自然地过渡到被搅乱的心。

normal.en: Up plus set: set it up so it tips over.
normal.cn: up 加 set：把东西顶起来直到翻倒。

normal.en: Be upset about something is the emotional frame learners need most.
normal.cn: be upset about 是学习者最需要的情绪框架。

normal.en: Upset is irregular: upset, upset, upset.
normal.cn: upset 的三态同形：upset、upset、upset。

normal.en: An upset stomach and a major upset show the two noun senses.
normal.cn: an upset stomach 与 a major upset 展示了两种名词义。

normal.en: Upsetting is the adjective for what causes the feeling.
normal.cn: upsetting 是表示「令人心烦」的形容词。

abstract.en: Nudge a cup with your elbow and watch it tip.
abstract.cn: 用手肘碰一下杯子，看它倒下。

abstract.en: See a chess board pushed an inch off the table.
abstract.cn: 看见棋盘被推离桌沿一点点。

abstract.en: Feel a plan come apart in the space of one phone call.
abstract.cn: 体会一个计划在一通电话里散架。

examples.en: Do not upset the tray when you leave the room.
examples.cn: 出房间时别把托盘碰翻。

examples.en: He was upset for days after the interview.
examples.cn: 面试之后他难受了好几天。

examples.en: The young team upset the favourites in the semi-final.
examples.cn: 这支年轻球队在半决赛爆冷击败了夺冠热门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆塞特」——阿婆塞东西太用力，一下把瓶罐塞翻在地，全家都慌了神。

root: 中古英语 upsetten，由 up（向上）与 setten（放置）复合，原义「竖起、翻覆」，后经「打翻」引申出「打乱、使心烦、爆冷」等义

sensesIntro.en: One tip-over spreads from cups to plans, to a person's mood, to a stomach, to a final score.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次翻倒，从杯子蔓延到计划、人的心情、肠胃，以至终场比分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup knocked over at the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上被碰倒的一只杯子。

branches.en: The object branch: a container goes down on its side.
branches.cn: 物件分支：容器倒向一边。

branches.en: The feeling branch: a mind knocked off its base.
branches.cn: 情绪分支：心意被撞离了底座。

branches.en: The order branch: arrangements turned over.
branches.cn: 秩序分支：安排被翻乱。

branches.en: The contest branch: the expected result is overturned.
branches.cn: 比赛分支：被认定会赢的结局被推翻。

branches.en: The body and score branches: stomach and upset result.
branches.cn: 身体与比分分支：翻搅的肠胃与意外的结果。

intro.en: Two of the commonest English words joined in one verb, with forms that never change.
intro.cn: 两个最常见的英语词合为一个动词，形态从不变化。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb behind the idea is evertere, to turn out or overturn.
latinIntro.cn: 这一概念背后的拉丁动词是 evertere（翻出、推翻）。

The cat knocked over the vase.

items.exampleCN: 这是一部让人不安的电影。

definition_zh: 城市的；都市的；城镇的；具有城市特点的
definition_en: relating to a town or city and to life in it
core_image: 傍晚一片连成线的窗灯
scene: 公交车在高架桥上慢慢挪动，两边楼群一路亮到天边。Air quality in urban areas is a constant concern.
sceneCN: 这里 urban 是「城市的」（第 1 个义项：与城市有关的）；句意为城区的空气质量一直是令人担心的事。连成线的窗灯，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 由 urban 加 -ization 构成名词，义为「城市化」
由 urban 加 -ize 构成动词，义为「使城市化」
同源但语义分化，义为「文雅的；有都市风度的」
同源名词，义为「郊区」，sub- 表示「靠近、在下」

senses.title: Belonging to a town or city
senses.definition: connected with a town or city rather than the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 与城镇或城市相关，而非乡村
senses.example: Urban areas grew quickly in the last decade.
senses.exampleCN: 过去十年城区扩展得很快。
senses.why: The adjective comes from the Latin word for city, so its first job is simply to mark what belongs to a city.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词源自拉丁语「城」一词，因此首要功能就是标出「属于城市的」。

senses.title: Characteristic of city living
senses.definition: used of habits, problems, or styles typical of city life
senses.definitionCN: 形容城市生活特有的习惯、问题或风格
senses.example: Noise and crowding are urban problems.
senses.exampleCN: 噪音和拥挤是城市的问题。
senses.why: Once a district exists, the habits that grow in it carry the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 城区一旦形成，在其中长出来的习惯也就带着同一个形容词。

senses.title: Relating to city government or services
senses.definition: used of the services and authorities of a city
senses.definitionCN: 形容城市的公共服务与市政机构
senses.example: Urban water supply was restored on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 城区供水星期一恢复了。
senses.why: The adjective marks whatever belongs to a city, and the city's own offices belong to it most directly.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出属于城市的事物，而市政府本身最直接地属于它。

senses.title: Designed for dense settlement
senses.definition: used of land used for buildings and roads rather than farming
senses.definitionCN: 形容用于建筑与道路而非耕作的土地
senses.example: Urban land costs far more than farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 城市用地比农田贵得多。
senses.why: The same city picture works on the ground itself: land inside the city is marked out for buildings.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅城市图景落在土地上：城里的地标出来是给房子用的。

senses.title: Polished in manner, in one old sense
senses.definition: an older sense describing refined manners, now kept in the word urbane
senses.definitionCN: 旧义指举止风雅，如今主要见于 urbane 一词
senses.example: His manners were urban in the older sense of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 按这个词的旧义，他的举止相当文雅。
senses.why: City life was once thought to polish people, so the adjective briefly praised good manners as well.
senses.whyCN: 人们一度认为城市生活能使人变得文雅，因此这个形容词也曾用来称赞好举止。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of the city, borrowed straight into English in its original shape.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语的「城市」形容词，几乎以原形直接借入英语。

items.en: Urbs meant a city, and urbanus meant of a city or belonging to city life.
items.cn: urbs 意为「城市」，urbanus 意为「城市的、都市生活的」。

items.en: Urbanus also came to describe manners thought polished in the city.
items.cn: urbanus 也渐渐用来形容在城里养成的风雅举止。

items.en: The adjective passed through French as urbain before reaching English.
items.cn: 这个形容词经由法语 urbain 再进入英语。

items.en: Urban enters English in the seventeenth century as a plain adjective of the city.
items.cn: urban 于十七世纪进入英语，是朴素的「城市的」形容词。

items.en: Its relatives multiply: urbane for manners, urbanization for a process.
items.cn: 同源词此后增多：urbane 指风度，urbanization 指过程。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin city root, while the near-meaning group compares terms of settlement and land.
note.cn: 形近组汇集建在拉丁「城」词根上的词，近义组比较聚落与土地类词。

normalIntro.en: One Latin root for the city, shared with suburb and urbane.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语「城」的词根，与 suburb、urbane 同出。

normal.en: Urb- means city: urban, suburb, urbane all contain it.
normal.cn: urb- 意为「城」：urban、suburb、urbane 都含着它。

normal.en: Urban planning and urban areas are the fixed phrases.
normal.cn: urban planning 与 urban areas 是固定搭配。

normal.en: The opposite is rural, not suburban.
normal.cn: 它的反面是 rural，不是 suburban。

normal.en: Urbane looks similar but means polished in manner.
normal.cn: urbane 长得像，意思是「文雅的」。

normal.en: Urbanization names the process, urbanize the verb.
